22652-a-campfire-girl-s-test-of-friendsh.description: A book by Jane L. Stewart. "No, because it ended well, Bessie. But if those girls in the camp next door had had their way, we wouldn't have had a single pleasant thing to remember about staying here, would we?"

arxiv-2106-08067.title: Stochastic fluctuations in protein interaction networks are nearly Poissonian.
arxiv-2106-08067.creator: Jaroslav Albert jaroslav.albert@ronininstitute.org
arxiv-2106-08067.description: Abstract Gene regulatory networks are comprised of biochemical reactions, which are inherently stochastic. Each reaction channel contributes to this stochasticity in different measure. In this paper we study the stochastic dynamics of protein interaction networks (PIN) that are made up of monomers and dimers. The network is defined by the dimers, which are formed by hybridizing two monomers.

arxiv-2108-12268.title: Fe XVII 2 ​ p ​ – ​ 3 ​ s 2p\mbox{ -- }3s line ratio diagnostic of shock formation radius in O stars
arxiv-2108-12268.creator: Gabriel J. Grell, Maurice A. Leutenegger, Chintan Shah
arxiv-2108-12268.description: Abstract The 2 ​ p ​ – ​ 3 ​ s 2p\mbox{ -- }3s lines of Fe XVII in the X-ray spectrum of the O-type star ζ \zeta Puppis exhibit an anomalous (3G + M2) / (3F) line ratio of ∼ 1.4 \sim 1.4 , in comparison with ∼ 2.4 \sim 2.4 for almost all other collisionally excited astrophysical spectra.

arxiv-2406-05876.title: Zero-Shot End-To-End Spoken Question Answering In Medical Domain
arxiv-2406-05876.creator: Yanis Labrak, Adel Moumen, Richard Dufour, Mickael Rouvier
arxiv-2406-05876.description: Abstract In the rapidly evolving landscape of spoken question-answering (SQA), the integration of large language models (LLMs) has emerged as a transformative development. Conventional approaches often entail the use of separate models for question audio transcription and answer selection, resulting in significant resource utilization and error accumulation.

arxiv-2410-20054.title: Evaluating Neural Networks for Early Maritime Threat Detection
arxiv-2410-20054.creator: Dhanush Tella, Chandra Teja Tiriveedhi, Naphtali Rishe
arxiv-2410-20054.description: Abstract Abstract : We consider the task of classifying trajectories of boat activities as a proxy for assessing maritime threats. Previous approaches have considered entropy-based metrics for clustering boat activity into three broad categories: random walk, following, and chasing. Here, we comprehensively assess the accuracy of neural network-based approaches as alternatives to entropy-based clustering.

arxiv-2412-03525.title: Pin classes II: Small pin classes
arxiv-2412-03525.creator: Robert Brignall, Ben Jarvis
arxiv-2412-03525.description: Abstract Pin permutations play an important role in the structural study of permutation classes, most notably in relation to simple permutations and well-quasi-ordering, and in enumerative consequences arising from these. In this paper, we continue our study of pin classes , which are permutation classes that comprise all the finite subpermutations contained in an infinite pin permutation.

pmc-10621625.title: Vigabatrin (Sabril) for the Treatment of Refractory Complex Focal Seizures in Adults: Pharmacologic and Clinical Considerations
pmc-10621625.creator: Taylor N Gatson, Orlandria A Freemont, Rachel L Coleman, Stewart J Lockett, Noah J Spillers, Shahab Ahmadzadeh, Omar Viswanath, Giustino Varrassi, Sahar Shekoohi, Alan D Kaye
pmc-10621625.description: To review the pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and adverse effects of vigabatrin (Sabril) and its role in managing refractory focal unaware seizures in adults. In the present investigation, a search of English-language literature from 1999 through 2023 was conducted using vigabatrin and Sabril as search terms to identify relevant studies and review articles.

pmc-11291847.title: CCL28 promotes progression of hepatocellular carcinoma through PDGFD-regulated MMP9 and VEGFA pathways
pmc-11291847.creator: Youyi Liu, Xingyi Chen, Xiading Zhang, Jingrou Guo, Yifei Tang, Cheng Jin, Minchen Wu
pmc-11291847.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health concern with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Chemokines have emerged as critical regulators in the progression and metastasis of HCC. This study aims to investigate the mechanisms involved in CCL28-promoted progression of HCC and provide novel therapeutic targets for HCC treatment.

pmc-11324668.title: Cancer/testis antigen expression and co-expression patterns in gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma
pmc-11324668.creator: Sukumar Kalvapudi, Akhil Goud Pachimatla, R. J. Seager, Jeffrey Conroy, Sarabjot Pabla, Sarbajit Mukherjee
pmc-11324668.description: Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEAC) poses a significant challenge due to its poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Recently, Cancer/testis antigens (CTAs) have emerged as potential therapy targets due to their high expression in tumor cells and their immunogenic nature. We aimed to explore the expression and co-expression of CTAs in GEAC.

pmc-11340095.title: Orthodontic movement after regenerative endodontic procedure in mature permanent tooth associated with dens invaginatus: a case report with 4-year follow-up
pmc-11340095.creator: Isabella Martínez, Rodrigo Oyonarte, Guillermo Concha, Claudia Brizuela
pmc-11340095.description: BackgroundRegenerative endodontic procedures (REPs) are innovative treatments aimed at restoring damaged dental structures. However, the effect of orthodontic movement on REP-treated teeth is not well understood and may have significant long-term consequences. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of orthodontic movement on a mature permanent tooth associated with dens invaginatus that has undergone a regenerative endodontic procedure (REP).

pmc-11394726.title: Optimal Humanized Scg3-Neutralizing Antibodies for Anti-Angiogenic Therapy of Diabetic Retinopathy
pmc-11394726.creator: Chengchi Huang, Prabuddha Waduge, Avinash Kaur, Hong Tian, Christina Y. Weng, John Timothy Stout, Iok-Hou Pang, Keith A. Webster, Wei Li
pmc-11394726.description: Secretogranin III (Scg3) is a diabetic retinopathy (DR)-restricted angiogenic factor identified in preclinical studies as a target for DR therapy. Previously, our group generated and characterized ML49.3, an anti-Scg3 monoclonal antibody (mAb) which we then converted into an EBP2 humanized antibody Fab fragment (hFab) with potential for clinical application. We also generated anti-Scg3 mT4 mAb and related EBP3 hFab.

pmc-12522353.title: Influence of induction of labor on morphological alterations in the pelvic floor after vaginal delivery determined by 4D transperineal ultrasound
pmc-12522353.creator: Jiao Yi, Zhiguo Tang, Leilei Wang, Bin Zhang, Xianxia Chen, Xiaoying Liu
pmc-12522353.description: BackgroundTo evaluate whether induction of labor increases pelvic floor morphology alterations in terms of a larger levator hiatus area or presence of levator ani muscle avulsion and compartment prolapse after vaginal delivery based on 4D tomographic ultrasound imaging.Materials and methodsThe retrospective study included 676 women who delivered in our maternal medical center between February 2024 to March 2025.

pmc-12558837.title: Inflammation-related biomarkers and berberine therapy in post-stroke depression: evidence from bioinformatics, machine learning, and experimental validation
pmc-12558837.creator: Wei Liu, Ruheng Wei, Jingya Xu, Zhilong Liu, Yulai Li
pmc-12558837.description: ObjectivePost-stroke depression (PSD), a common neuropsychiatric complication, significantly hinders stroke recovery and quality of life. Given the established role of inflammation in the pathogenesis of PSD, this study aimed to identify key inflammation-related genes and pathways using bioinformatics and machine learning and further evaluate the protective effects of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) monomer compounds.

pmc-12985134.title: Potential Links Between Aging, Mitochondrial Dysfunction, and Drug Transporter Function—Molecular Mechanisms and Pharmacokinetic Implications
pmc-12985134.creator: Patryk Rzeczycki, Oliwia Pęciak, Martyna Plust, Marek Droździk
pmc-12985134.description: Aging is associated with complex physiological changes that influence drug pharmacokinetics, including alterations in mitochondrial function and gastrointestinal (GI) drug transporter activity. Mitochondrial dysfunction—characterized by reduced oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial DNA damage, and increased reactive oxygen species—is a hallmark of aging and may affect energy- and redox-dependent cellular processes in the gut.

pmc-13079337.title: Integrative genomic analysis identifies key target genes and candidate drugs for spinal stenosis
pmc-13079337.creator: Demeng Xia, Yongjie Chen, Rui Wu, Yifan Tang, Yanqing Sun, Xiongsheng Chen
pmc-13079337.description: BackgroundSpinal stenosis is a common pathological condition characterized by the narrowing of the spinal canal, contributing to substantial morbidity and imposing a significant socioeconomic burden. Despite its clinical importance, the genetic drivers and cellular mechanisms driving its progression remain inadequately understood, necessitating integrative approaches to identify therapeutic targets.MethodsThis study employed an integrative multi-omics strategy.

pmc-13095623.title: Objective physical activity characteristics and long-term functional disability trajectories in community-dwelling older adults: the amplifying risk of stroke
pmc-13095623.creator: Jianhui Pan, Zanzhi Wang, Yaoquan He, Shuang Liu, Kao Zhang, Jinliang Peng, Chun Xu, Jun Zhang, Peng Huang
pmc-13095623.description: BackgroundFunctional decline is a major challenge in aging, particularly for those with a history of cerebrovascular events. Yet, prior research relies heavily on self-reported measures. The impact of objective physical activity patterns, particularly sedentary accumulation, on long-term functional prognosis remains unclear.MethodsUsing the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS), we analyzed 480 community-dwelling older adults (weighted N = 1.9 million).

pmc-13427727.title: Circulating tumour cell-derived xenograft as a preclinical platform for metastatic breast cancer
pmc-13427727.creator: Zuzana Kahounová, Markéta Hrušková, Stanislav Drápela, Ondřej Naar, Ráchel Víchová, Jiří Navrátil, Pavel Fabian, Filip Zavadil Kokáš, Aleš Hampl, Jan Bouchal, Karel Souček
pmc-13427727.description: BackgroundCirculating tumour cells (CTCs) are mediators of cancer dissemination and the formation of metastasis, which is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths. Experimental models derived from CTCs contribute to understanding the biology of CTCs, their role in dissemination, and the discovery of potential drugs targeting CTCs.

pmc-13566172.title: LEAP2 Regulates Insulin Secretion from INS-1E Beta Cells and Rat Pancreatic Islets: An In Vitro Study
pmc-13566172.creator: Oskar Sosiński, Ewa Pruszyńska-Oszmałek, Maciej Sassek, Natalia Leciejewska, Piotr Pawlak, Paweł Antoni Kołodziejski
pmc-13566172.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). LEAP2 is an endogenous antagonist and inverse agonist of GHSR-1a, the receptor for acyl-ghrelin. Although LEAP2 is increasingly recognized as a regulator of appetite and glucose homeostasis, its direct effects on pancreatic endocrine cells remain incompletely understood. The present in vitro study evaluated whether LEAP2 modulates insulin secretion and the expression of insulin-related genes in INS-1E beta cells and isolated rat pancreatic islets. LEAP2 treatment altered selected components of the insulin-related expression profile in a model- and time-dependent manner.
